judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) instead of the parsed data, and this call site stores that envelope verbatim as credential.key where the replaced code stored googleCredentialSchema.parse()'s data. On the default sharing-disabled path, the first Google token refresh writes {success:true,data:{...}} into Credential.key, so every subsequent load reads credential.key.access_token and refresh_token as undefined and all Google Calendar operations fail; the stored OAuth tokens are effectively lost and every Google user must reconnect.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result object (the Zod envelope `{ success, data, error? }`) rather than the parsed `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new code assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously it stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the parsed credential object), so this change would store the envelope into `Credential.key`, breaking later code that expects `credential.key.access_token`, `refresh_token`, etc. This is directly verifiable from the diff and would cause Google Calendar credential refresh/storage to malfunction.
